Legendary graphic designer Susan Kare recently gave a talk at the Startup School 2026 event. Her presentation video has been uploaded to Y Combinator's YouTube channel, and you can watch it below.

Susan Kare shared many wonderful stories and design insights.

It has been over 40 years since the original Macintosh was launched, but the system's graphics, fonts, icons, and overall UI elements remain just as appealing today as they were back then.

In fact, many of the elements Susan Kare designed for the original Macintosh are still part of macOS today, preserved both in spirit and in appearance. From the Command key symbol and the "Happy Mac" startup icon, to the system fonts and the hand-shaped cursor, Kare's work not only shaped the Mac's visual language, but also influenced the entire personal computer industry.

Although anyone who has studied Apple's history should have seen Kare's sketches, and may have seen or heard her talk about these early works in interviews, hearing her share in person — from that era when the graphical user interface and pixel art were still uncharted territory — the passion and frustration of that work remains incredibly compelling.

So, if you're interested in design, curious about Apple's history, or simply want to hear a professional share a lifetime of passion, Kare's talk is absolutely not to be missed.

In addition to detailing her work at Apple, Kare also shared how she came to join the company, showcased some of her work created after she left, shared various anecdotes from Apple's early days, and quoted other legendary designers to bring further inspiration to the audience.
